newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian farmers urge subsidy protection.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian farmers urge subsidy protection.

text.p: Australian farmers said on Thursday they were sceptical about U.S. President Bill Clinton's pledge to protect them from the impact of agricultural subsidies.
Clinton said during his visit to Canberra on Wednesday he had made a commitment that free trade nations would not be hurt by the use of export subsidies.
The National Farmers Federation was hopeful that Clinton would protect Australian farmers from the battle between the U.S. and Europe over agricultural subsidies, it said in a statement.

The NFF said it took heart from the fact that the Export Enhancement Programme (EEP), which subsidises U.S. grain sales, had not been used to subsidise U.S. wheat exports for the past month, despite the Europeans continuing use of export subsidies.

"Such U.S. restraint at the moment is most welcome, and we would hope that with that sort of leadership, we can train our attention on the Europeans, in an effort to push them back from using export subsidies too vigorously," it said.
Washington says its export subsidies, such as EEP, are aimed at countering subsidies by the European Union and not at breaking into traditional Australian markets.
The federation said the U.S. should go one step further with trade liberalisation and completely dismantle the EEP and Dairy Export Incentive Programme, which subsidises dairy sales.

Federation president Donald McGauchie said he was encouraged by Clinton's proposal to raise issues of free and fair trade at the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation (APEC) forum in the Philippines next week.
